truths.CP2:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM leads AS l
JOIN opportunities AS o ON o.lead_id = l.lead_id
WHERE l.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND l.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
  AND o.is_won
  AND o.closed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
truths.CP4:
WITH won AS (
  -- one row: the won deals of the leads from the five paid sources created in the first half of 2025
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS won
  FROM leads AS l
  JOIN opportunities AS o ON o.lead_id = l.lead_id
  WHERE l.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND l.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
    AND l.source IN ('display', 'events', 'paid_search', 'paid_social', 'review_sites')
    AND o.is_won
),
spend AS (
  -- one row: the paid media of January to June 2025
  SELECT SUM(spend_eur) AS spend
  FROM marketing_spend_monthly
  WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND month < DATE '2025-07-01'
)
SELECT ROUND(s.spend / w.won, 2)
FROM spend AS s
CROSS JOIN won AS w

CP1.explanation: Fixing the cohort by the lead's date and following its later stages to the end of the data gives every source the same chance; starting from opportunities mixes in leads from other months.

CP5.explanation: The cost holds paid media only, so a cost of 0 means no media spend, not a free deal; and the most deals or the most leads do not make a source the cheapest way to win one.
